pairs.subject: test-harness
pairs.evidence: crates/table-verify/src/acceptance.rs:2 The acceptance matrix only sees tests in the cargo workspace graph, so the vitest tests that carry U2, U3, U4, W1 and W7 (fontFloor.test.ts, modeBadge*.test.tsx, NoteChip.test.tsx, routeRestore.test.tsx, withdraw.render.test.tsx) are outside its population, and the CI-published matrix shows those IDs as having no test even though tests exist.

techniques.evidence: crates/table-verify/src/acceptance.rs:2 The matrix reads `--workspace` as if it covered the whole repo, but apps/desktop/client tests are not cargo members. A grep found no Rust test named u2_/u3_/u4_/w1_/w7_, so those rows read 'none'.
crates/table-verify/src/acceptance.rs:174 The headline count does not name the suite it was measured over (Rust cargo tests only), so it reads as covering every test the repo has.
crates/table-verify/src/acceptance_main.rs:13 Membership comes from test names. An input that lists zero tests exits 2 instead of green, which is the floor the technique asks for.
crates/table-verify/src/acceptance.rs:310 The text walk of the design docs checks the ID list in both directions and declares a floor on what it found.
crates/table-verify/src/authority_tests.rs:449 The enumeration publishes its engagement: the agreement test proves it ran on every cell, not on an empty set.

crates/table-verify/src/authority_tests.rs:211 The failing case is paired with the same step passing once its one precondition holds, so the assertion is shown to discriminate. This is an input-side control, not a production mutation.

pairs.subject: test-harness
pairs.evidence: apps/desktop/client/src/design/tokens.test.ts:56 The 'every token is read' walk searches raw file text with comments left in, so prose like the tokens.css:86 comment `font-stretch: var(--label-stretch)` (and the one at fonts.css:7) counts as a read: delete every real use of a token and the test still passes as long as a comment mentions it.

techniques.evidence: apps/desktop/client/src/design/tokens.test.ts:56 The search space holds both code and prose about the code: comments are not stripped here, though the colour-literal walk in the same file does strip them. Also, the SCALE_OR_PINNED exemption list (line 45) is never checked in the reverse direction, and the CSS walks declare no floor.
